rationale: The two summed scale legs are on wildly different scales (annual asset growth is O(0.1–1) while prstkc/at is O(0.01)), so the composite will be numerically dominated by asset growth and end up a near-duplicate of the archive's ExpansionFundingSource rather than the claimed "breadth" test.

A legitimate single-lever ablation that replaces the rank-difference gate with the economically literal funding surplus and thereby diagnoses whether the winner's alpha comes from measured self-funding or from an embedded profitability (RMW-like) rank, though its novelty is limited and the raw-times-raw product will be outlier-sensitive despite the winsorization.

Swapping RANK for IND_RANK in an existing strong signal is a standard mechanical neutralization rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the archive already contains industry-conditioned gates (IND_ZSCORE), so the expected information gain is cosmetic.

The scale leg (dividends + buybacks + net debt retirement, scaled by assets) is essentially the sign-flipped Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan net-external-financing / total-payout measure, so the signal risks rediscovering a published anomaly dressed in a gate that itself re-uses equity issuance and thus double-counts financing direction.

Genuinely explores financing-policy instability rather than level and pairs it with an untried quality dimension, but the 5-year volatility of scaled net financing is mechanically tied to size/age and the gate is literally negated Novy-Marx gross profitability, so a strong result may be a size-times-known-profitability composite rather than the proposed mechanism.

Since the same issuance scale with the opposite retained-earnings gate already produced a strongly negative FMB slope in the archive, a negative slope here would most likely just reflect the base external-financing anomaly rather than the claimed "unexpected raise by mature firms" channel, making the two gate directions mutually uninformative.
